text: Every exact verdict so far needed all 24 known letters to agree with the method. Sanborn enciphered by hand and admits he was sloppy: a wrong row at one or two of those places would have thrown away the right answer.

A repeating key on the sculpture's tables, every length 1-26, letting 1, 2 or 3 known letters disagree; every surviving setting read by quadgrams and by the blind judge, K4's readings and 20 scrambled copies' together, with three planted slipped messages.

Nothing fits below length 25 on K4 or below 24 on any copy, even with 3 slips; at 24-26 too few checks remain to decide and settings fit everywhere. K4's best reading scores 3, below the copies' 8; the plants score 88, 85, 82 and are found.
